note: Both sets cover the same wiring-schedule rows (20, 31, 32, 33, 34, 50, 150, 151) with essentially identical, mostly correct bindings of conductor material, conductor size and conduit size, and both share the same defects: the '#12/2WG.' description is bound to item 151 although the schedule shows it under symbol 10 (151 is 'AL: 3#4/0, ARMORED CABLE'), the 'AL: 3#4/0, ARMORED CABLE' quote is attached to item 150, and one claim uses the vague entity 'cable'. The only real difference is that A adds a spurious 'conditions: C.' to three conduit-size claims (C. is just the abbreviation for conduit in the description, not an operating condition), while B states those claims cleanly. Coverage of the notes (main panel 120/240V, 150A/2P main breaker, 200A/2P NFDS NEMA 3R, 4 AWG copper to gnd, L1/L2/N no gnd) is absent from both.
remarks: Text layer is badly jumbled around the wiring schedule (symbol numbers appear out of order and 151 appears twice), so row-to-description binding must be read from the image: 151=AL 3#4/0 ARMORED CABLE, 150=AL 3#4/0 #4G. 2-1/2"C., 50=CU 3#6 #8G. 1"C., 34=CU 6#10 3#10G. 1"C., 33=CU 6#10 #10G. 1"C., 32=CU 2#10USE-2, 31=CU 2#10 #10G. 3/4"C., 20=CU 3#12 #12G. 3/4"C., 10=CU #12/2WG. Both extractions make the same two row-binding errors (151/10 and the 150/151 quote), which is why the wrong counts are equal; the sets differ only in A's meaningless 'conditions: C.' field. Both also omit the NOTES block (main panel rating, main breaker, NFDS/enclosure) and the interface wiring notes (4 AWG copper to gnd; L1, L2 & N, no gnd).
